This could be avoided by always outputting exactly one valid JSON command and keeping any reasoning internal. If playing again: I’d first do a fast sweep of all edges for serial number, batteries, indicators, and ports before attempting any module, then tackle the fastest modules. I’d standardize callouts (timer, strikes, module LED state) every time and avoid any non-JSON output.
Lessons learned: In collaborative real-time puzzles, strict protocol compliance and concise, structured observations matter as much as puzzle knowledge. Early collection of global bomb info reduces back-and-forth, and confirming outcomes (strike/LED) immediately prevents compounding errors.
